final_answer:
Let
\[
X=U_{(r)},\qquad Y=U_{(s)}.
\]
I claim
\[
\rho_{r,s}^{(n)}
=\sqrt{\frac{r(n+1-s)}{s(n+1-r)}}.
\]

For \(a,b>0\), let \(\pi_k^{a,b}\) be the monic degree \(k\) polynomial orthogonal to all lower-degree polynomials in \(L^2(\operatorname{Beta}(a,b))\). Here
\[
X\sim \operatorname{Beta}(r,n+1-r),\qquad
Y\sim \operatorname{Beta}(s,n+1-s).
\]

Conditioning on \(Y=y\), the \(r\)-th order statistic among the \(s-1\) points below \(y\) satisfies
\[
X=yZ,\qquad Z\sim \operatorname{Beta}(r,s-r),
\]
independently of \(y\). Therefore, for each \(k\),
\[
E[\pi_k^{r,n+1-r}(X)\mid Y=y]
\]
is a degree \(k\) polynomial in \(y\). It is orthogonal to every polynomial in \(y\) of degree \(<k\), because conditioning the other way makes such a polynomial in \(Y\) become a polynomial in \(X\) of degree \(<k\). Its leading coefficient is
\[
E[Z^k]=\frac{(r)_k}{(s)_k}.
\]
Thus
\[
E[\pi_k^{r,n+1-r}(X)\mid Y]
=
\frac{(r)_k}{(s)_k}\pi_k^{s,n+1-s}(Y).
\]

Similarly, conditioning on \(X=x\),
\[
Y=x+(1-x)W,\qquad W\sim \operatorname{Beta}(s-r,n+1-s),
\]
so the leading coefficient in \(x\) is
\[
E[(1-W)^k]=\frac{(n+1-s)_k}{(n+1-r)_k}.
\]
Hence
\[
E[\pi_k^{s,n+1-s}(Y)\mid X]
=
\frac{(n+1-s)_k}{(n+1-r)_k}\pi_k^{r,n+1-r}(X).
\]

After normalizing these orthogonal polynomials, the singular values of the conditional expectation operator are
\[
\lambda_k
=
\sqrt{
\frac{(r)_k(n+1-s)_k}{(s)_k(n+1-r)_k}
},
\qquad k\ge 0.
\]
The \(k=0\) value corresponds to constants. Since \(f,g\) are required to have mean \(0\), only \(k\ge1\) matters.

For \(k\ge1\),
\[
\lambda_k^2
=
\prod_{j=0}^{k-1}
\frac{r+j}{s+j}\cdot
\frac{n+1-s+j}{n+1-r+j}.
\]
Every factor is \(<1\), so
\[
\lambda_k^2\le
\frac{r}{s}\cdot \frac{n+1-s}{n+1-r}
=\lambda_1^2.
\]
Therefore the maximal possible covariance is \(\lambda_1\), attained by the normalized linear functions of \(X\) and \(Y\). Hence
\[
\boxed{\rho_{r,s}^{(n)}
=
\sqrt{\frac{r(n+1-s)}{s(n+1-r)}}}.
\]

As a check, for \(n=2,r=1,s=2\), this gives \(\rho=1/2\), which is exactly the ordinary correlation of the minimum and maximum of two independent uniform variables.
